transport.access: Bearer Authorization header injected from tokenStore localStorage on each http request.
transport.refresh: POST /auth/refresh JSON body {refreshToken}; raw axios against API_BASE_URL, bypassing the shared response interceptor.
transport.cookieEvidence: No auth Set-Cookie or withCredentials usage found in bounded frontend/backend source. Backend CORS credentials:true and any cookie-related deployment flags alone do not establish cookie auth support.
transport.config: VITE_API_BASE_URL, default /api, configures frontend API root. JWT_ACCESS_TTL/JWT_ACCESS_TTL_SEC and JWT_REFRESH_TTL configure server token lifetimes; response expiresIn is separate and historical R02 reports fixed 7200 values. This TTL matter is adjacent, not decided by RP00-T04.

observedCurrentBehavior.behavior: Module-local inflight Promise coalesces refresh in one JS module instance; each original request is replayed once after success.

observedCurrentBehavior.scenario: two tabs refresh the same family/token concurrently
observedCurrentBehavior.behavior: Each tab has its own inflight Promise. Server reads an unrevoked token then unconditionally updates revokedAt and independently creates a random-family successor. Historical R02 recorded two successful successors under the controlled interleaving; no current dynamic rerun.

observedCurrentBehavior.scenario: old refresh failure after another tab wrote a successor
observedCurrentBehavior.behavior: Refreshing tab's catch unconditionally clears shared localStorage tokens and broadcasts expiry; it does not compare the failed refresh token or generation to the currently stored session.

observedCurrentBehavior.scenario: old refresh success after login/session switch to user B
observedCurrentBehavior.behavior: refreshAccessToken writes the response to global tokenStore without checking who initiated it; a late response can replace B's shared token pair.

observedCurrentBehavior.scenario: A's original request replay after session changes to B
observedCurrentBehavior.behavior: On replay, request interceptor reads the current global access token. If B's token is current, the original Axios config can be sent with B's Bearer token; no initiating actor/session generation is attached to the request config.

Only 401 with AUTH_EXPIRED or INVALID_TOKEN enters refresh. Other 401 clears global token state; 403 is thrown without clearing/refreshing; no-response network errors return NETWORK_ERROR without clearing tokens. No offline authorization fallback is in this HTTP client path.

observedCurrentBehavior.scenario: server actor binding and access-token invalidation
observedCurrentBehavior.behavior: Refresh row determines user and signs access token for that row.user. Bearer middleware verifies JWT and current user status, but does not consume passwordChangedAt or a session generation/version. D-S01-04 remains a separate pending policy gate.

requirements: Capture immutable initiating actor and session generation for every protected request and its refresh operation.
Accept a refresh success only if its originating session lineage is still current; an old success must never overwrite a later login or account switch.
Apply refresh failure cleanup only if the failed lineage still owns current storage; stale failures must not erase a successor session.
Replay only under the initiating actor/session lineage. If that identity changed, fail closed and do not send the original request with the new user's credential.
Coordinate concurrent refresh across tabs or use an equivalent approved protocol; define server-side single-consumer CAS/family replay behavior and loser response jointly with the client.
An expired-access 401 may trigger one bounded refresh; 403 must remain authorization denial; network/offline errors must not be represented as auth failure or clear valid tokens.
Define supported transport and compatibility window from evidence. Do not treat CORS credential flags as cookie transport support.
designChoiceStillRequired: Named security/auth/frontend owners select cross-tab coordination and fallback behavior.
Named security/auth owner selects refresh token single-consumption, family replay/theft response, rotation retry/idempotency window, and failure recovery semantics.
Named approver records exact supported clients/transport, compatibility window, residual risks and approval date/evidence.
D-S01-04 separately decides access JWT invalidation after password/reset/privilege changes; RP00-T04 does not choose it.

scenarios: same-family two-tab simultaneous refresh: one current lineage remains, loser response per approved policy
old refresh failure arriving after new successor is stored: successor remains unchanged
old refresh success arriving after logout and B login: B session remains unchanged
A's original mutation 401 arriving after B login: request is not replayed with B credential and server actor remains A or request is safely aborted
current genuinely invalid refresh: only that current generation is cleared and session expiry surfaced
403 and offline/network failure: no refresh, no cross-identity replay, no clearing of a valid generation
